name: Pick
text: Focus on Reddit’s r/MachineLearning and r/artificial subreddits first. They’re high-signal, low-noise, and already curated by AI-curious engineers who post links with context. Trade-off: we miss niche Telegram groups, but Reddit’s search and comment threads let us verify relevance faster than scrolling through scattered chats.

name: Assay
text: Reddit’s curation is a false high-signal: it’s biased toward Western, English-speaking engineers, missing non-English, non-tech, or non-engineer voices that still shape AI adoption. Better alternative: sample Telegram’s AI channels (e.g., AI Hub, Future of AI) where raw, unfiltered discussions reveal gaps Reddit ignores. Settle it by comparing the top 10 AI trends from each source—if Telegram’s list differs by >30%, Reddit is too narrow.

name: Assay
text: Telegram’s "raw, unfiltered" noise is a false solution—it buries signal under spam, bots, and non-English chatter that’s harder to verify than Reddit’s upvoted links. Better: split the sample—Telegram for *adoption pain points* (where unfiltered voices matter) and Reddit for *technical signals* (where curation filters noise). Settle it by measuring: if Telegram yields 3x more irrelevant posts than Reddit’s curated threads, default to Reddit.
